subject: chemistry
title: Transition metals
key_idea: Most metals are transition metals. They are harder, stronger and denser than the Group 1 metals, with high melting points, and are less reactive. Many have ions with different charges, form coloured compounds and are useful as catalysts.

blocks.text: (Separate science only) The transition metals are the block of elements between Group 2 and Group 3. This section compares them with the alkali metals.

items.meaning: A metal in the central block of the periodic table, such as chromium (Cr), manganese (Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt (Co), nickel (Ni) and copper (Cu).
A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up.

rows: Reactivity with oxygen, water and halogens

items: The transition metals have similar properties to each other, which are different from those of Group 1.
Example: copper is harder and less reactive than sodium.
Transition metals have higher melting points and densities than Group 1 metals.
They are harder and stronger, and less reactive.

blocks.text: Many transition elements share three properties that Group 1 metals do not.

items: They have **ions with different charges**. Iron forms Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺ ions.
They form **coloured compounds**. Compounds of copper are often blue, and vanadium oxide, V₂O₅, is orange.
They are useful as **catalysts**. Iron is a catalyst in making ammonia, vanadium(V) oxide is a catalyst in making sulfuric acid, and platinum is a catalyst in fuel cells.

diagram.alt: Sort each property into Group 1 metals, transition metals or both.

items: Many transition elements have ions with different charges.
Many are useful as catalysts, for example iron.

checks.q: Give two differences between the physical properties of the transition metals and those of the Group 1 metals.
checks.a: Any two from: transition metals have higher melting points, are denser, are harder, are stronger.

checks.q: State three typical properties of transition metals that Group 1 metals do not have.
checks.a: Ions with different charges, coloured compounds, and useful as catalysts.

checks.q: Platinum acts as a catalyst in a fuel cell. Explain how its position in the periodic table shows this.
checks.a: Platinum is a transition metal, and transition metals are useful as catalysts.

worked_example.question:
Tungsten is a transition metal. Potassium is a Group 1 metal.

Give two differences between the properties of tungsten and the properties of potassium.
answer_points: Tungsten has a higher melting or boiling point.
Tungsten has ions with different charges, forms coloured compounds, or can be a catalyst.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. The converse for potassium is also accepted.

worked_example.question:
In a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, hydrogen and oxygen react at the electrodes.

Platinum acts as a catalyst.

State, in terms of its position in the periodic table, why you would expect platinum to act as a catalyst.
answer_points: Platinum is a transition metal (or transition element).
worked_example.tip: Name the block of the periodic table that platinum is in. Irrelevant extra information is ignored.

worked_example.question:
The table shows information about the physical properties of four elements, W, X, Y and Z.

W: density 0.97 g/cm³, melting point 98 °C, conducts electricity
X: density 7.87 g/cm³, melting point 1538 °C, conducts electricity
Y: density 0.003 g/cm³, melting point −102 °C, does not conduct electricity
Z: density 1.74 g/cm³, melting point 650 °C, conducts electricity

One of the elements is a transition metal.

Compare the physical and chemical properties of Group 1 metals and transition metals.

Use the information in the table, and your own knowledge.
answer_points: Group 1 metals have a lower density and a lower melting point.
Group 1 metals are softer and less strong.
Both Group 1 metals and transition metals conduct electricity.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the physical points, plus the idea that Group 1 metals are more reactive. An unqualified answer is taken to refer to Group 1 metals.

worked_example.question:
One physical property of transition elements such as copper and cobalt is that they are hard.
Other metals such as lithium are softer.
State two other physical properties of copper and cobalt which are significantly different from lithium.

items: Transition elements are metals with high densities and high melting points. They often act as catalysts, both as elements and in their compounds.
(Supplement) Transition elements have ions with variable oxidation numbers. Iron forms iron(II), Fe²⁺, and iron(III), Fe³⁺.
